lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have one child, Alex, who's 13 years old and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. It's good to know you have Alex, who is 13 years old and living with you.

Now I need to ask: Are you currently living in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to ask about your immigration status:

Do you have the right to reside in the UK? (For example, are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status, indefinite leave to remain, or another immigration status that gives you the right to reside here?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have the right to reside in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I need to ask about Alex specifically:

Is Alex in full-time non-advanced education or approved training? (This would be relevant since Alex is 13, as children aged 16 and over need to meet certain education requirements to qualify.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex is only 13, so they're just in regular school - nothing special really, just normal secondary school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's perfect, thank you. Since Alex is 13 and in regular secondary school, that's absolutely fine for Child Benefit purposes.

Now I need to ask: Are you the person mainly responsible for Alex? This means you're the one who Alex lives with and who is primarily responsible for their care and upbringing.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. Alex lives with me and I'm the one taking care of them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment.

Is anyone else currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided:
- Alex is 13 years old (under 16)
- Alex lives with you in the UK
- You have the right to reside in the UK
- You are responsible for Alex's care
- Alex is in regular secondary school education
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

All the eligibility requirements are met, so you should be able to successfully claim Child Benefit for Alex. You can apply online through the government's official website or by post using the claim form.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
